name: Queen mate: walk the king in
note: Use the queen to box the king in, then bring your own king close. Always check that you leave the enemy king a square to move, or it is stalemate.

name: Queen mate in one (beware stalemate)
note: Qg8 is mate. Some other queen moves, like Qc7, are stalemate. Count the king's escape squares before you move.

name: Rook mate in one
note: Your king holds the squares in front, the rook checks on the back rank. Ra8 is mate.

name: Rook mate: cut off and shrink the box
note: Cut the king off with the rook, march your king up, and use the opposition to force it back one rank at a time.

name: Two bishops mate
note: Two bishops on neighbouring diagonals make a wall. Herd the king to the edge, then to a corner, and bring your king to help.

name: King and pawn: king in front wins
note: Your king stands two squares in front of the pawn on the 6th rank. Play Kd6 and keep the opposition and the pawn walks in.

name: Key square: reach it and win
note: d6 is a key square for the e4 pawn. If your king gets to a key square you win, wherever the enemy king is.

name: Defender in front of the pawn: draw
note: The black king sits right in front of the pawn and blocks it. Without a king ahead of the pawn you cannot win here.

name: Opposition: the side to move loses it
note: Kings face each other with one square between. You must move, so you lose the opposition and cannot make progress. Same position with Black to move is a win for White.

name: Win the opposition with Kd5
note: Kd5 takes the opposition and keeps the enemy king off the pawn's path. Wrong king moves let it draw.

name: Sidestep to gain the opposition
note: No pawn push works yet. Find a king move that takes the key squares in front of the pawn. Pushing too early draws.

name: Tempo moves (triangulation idea)
note: Several king moves win, but you must keep ahead of the pawn. The aim of triangulation is to lose a move so the other side is in zugzwang.

name: Rook pawn: draw by the corner
note: Wrong-coloured bishop: the bishop does not control a8, the queening square. Black heads for the corner and cannot be driven out. Draw.

name: Rook pawn on the 6th: stalemate trick
note: A rook pawn with the defender in the corner is a draw. If White pushes, the black king has no moves and it is stalemate.

name: Rule of the square
note: Draw an imaginary square from the pawn to its queening square. If the king can step into it, the pawn is caught. Kd6 does that.

name: Lucena position
note: Build a bridge: Rc4 and then Rb4, so your king can step out of the pawn's path and the rook blocks checks.

name: Philidor position (defence)
note: Keep your rook on the 6th rank so the enemy king cannot advance. When the pawn reaches the 6th, switch to checks from behind.

name: Rook behind the passed pawn
note: Rooks belong behind passed pawns, yours or theirs. The pawn can run while the rook protects it from behind.

name: Outside passed pawn
note: The a-pawn drags the enemy king away, then your king walks in to eat the kingside pawns. A far-away passed pawn is a huge asset.

name: Pawn breakthrough 3 v 3
note: Sacrifice one pawn to make a passed pawn: b6! forces a path through. Count the moves before you start.

name: Queen vs pawn on the 7th: win with checks
note: With a central pawn the queen wins by checking and pulling the king in front of the pawn, then your king arrives.

name: Queen vs rook pawn on the 7th: draw
note: A rook or bishop pawn on the 7th with its king nearby draws because of stalemate tricks. You need your own king close to win.

name: King, bishop and knight mate
note: Drive the king to the corner of your bishop's colour. Use the W-manoeuvre with the knight and bishop. It takes about 30 moves, so study it.

name: Opposite-coloured bishops: fortress draw
note: With bishops on opposite colours the defender often draws even a pawn down, by blocking pawns on the colour of their bishop.

name: Queen vs rook
note: Win by forks and skewers. The rook must stay protected by its king, so drive the king away from it.

name: King ahead of the pawn wins
note: Your king is in front of the pawn, so the enemy king cannot stop it. Push when the opposition is yours.

name: Pawn far ahead of its king: draw
note: The black king gets in front of the pawn first. A king behind its pawn cannot make progress.

name: Pawn behind the defender's king: draw
note: Black's king reaches the squares in front of the pawn and holds the opposition. Do not rush the pawn.

name: Win by taking the key squares
note: Your king is already on a key square in front of the pawn. Escort it up the board.

name: Pawn on the 5th with a supporting king
note: Your king leads the pawn. Keep it in front and avoid stalemate when the pawn gets to the 7th.
